anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : The optimizer persistently chooses a substantially sub-optimal execution plan even though statistics are acceptable.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : Physical pages or index structures are internally inconsistent with the logical contents of the database, leading to unreliable access paths and data retrieval.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly : A hard limit is reached on data files, temp areas, logs, or backup destinations, preventing further space allocation.

Composite definition: This anomaly represents the database instance in which (1) the optimizer is selecting poor plans, (2) underlying data and index pages are corrupted or inconsistent, and (3) the storage layer is at or beyond its space capacity—all at the same time while the workload is executing.

Combined anomalous phenomena: • Identical SQL statements oscillate between radically different plans; many fall back to full table scans because damaged indexes are marked unusable or return incorrect results. • Full scans, bad join orders, and loss of parallelism inflate I/O volume, temp-space usage, and redo generation, rapidly consuming the last free blocks in data, temp, and log areas. • Queries that do find and use corrupt indexes may return wrong or duplicate rows, causing application retries that drive even more log growth and temp spills. • Space-exhaustion errors ("cannot allocate extent", "log full", "temp space exhausted") interleave with corruption messages (checksum failures, key-order violations) and plan-cache invalidations, making the root cause set hard to distinguish. • Recovery or repair utilities abort mid-run because the required work space or logs cannot be extended, leaving additional orphaned segments and further plan instability.

Causal chain and interaction: Corrupted indexes mislead the optimizer, producing drastic mis-estimates that trigger sub-optimal plans and heavy resource usage. The inflated I/O, sort, and redo volume quickly depletes the already scarce storage, converting latent space pressure into hard allocation failures. In turn, space exhaustion prevents index rebuilds, online repair, or even clean checkpointing, allowing corruption to persist and spread. The sudden invalidation of unusable indexes forces the optimizer to re-optimize and often choose even less efficient plans, which further accelerates space growth, creating a vicious feedback loop that degrades both performance and data reliability.

entry.official_definition: Sets the interval between optional checks that the client is still connected while running queries.
entry.trigger_condition: During a long-running query, PostgreSQL polls the socket at this interval and can detect a closed connection sooner.
entry.workload_impact: Long-running queries can be aborted sooner after the kernel reports that the client connection is closed.
entry.default_behavior: Default value is 0, disabling connection checks.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
